If anything I just want to reiterate the importance of freshness in Japanese cuisine and food safety. I think it’s paramount that there are less pre-made items to encompass the omakase dining experience. My overall recommendation is to not visit this place until adequate change has been applied.

My friend and I arrived at Maki Nori in Soho on a Wednesday evening, joining a small group for an exclusive Chef's Counter Sushi Night to mark the launch of this new handroll restaurant in central London. The occasion brought us together with Chef Teddy Lee, founder of Maki & Ramen, who introduced his latest concept built around freshness, technique and quality ingredients. Tucked along a side street, the venue felt easy to find and welcoming from the first step inside.

The space leans into a calm, focused atmosphere. Warm lighting sits low over a polished chef's counter, where guests face the kitchen directly. Conversation flowed easily, the noise level stayed comfortable, and the pace felt unhurried despite the open kitchen energy. A dedicated dry-age fridge near the entrance signals the kitchen's craft-led approach before you even sit down. The room feels considered without being precious, suiting Soho's character.

The menu followed a clear sequence, beginning with crudos and moving through handrolls and a few hot plates.

The scallop with orange ponzu arrived clean and bright, the texture soft and the citrus measured. Hamachi with yuzu mint ponzu followed, balanced and cool, while the salmon with elderflower ponzu offered a gentler, floral finish.

Handrolls then came one by one, sliced, rolled and passed across the counter within seconds. The nori stayed crisp, the rice held warmth, and fillings like negi toro, snow crab and eel kept their distinct character. Tempura, gyoza and dynamite prawns added a welcome variety. Sourcing felt evident in every bite, from Hikido scallops to bluefin tuna from Spain and Scottish salmon, which justified the price point for a premium handroll experience in London.

We finished with a delicious strawberry custard tart, which was simply divine.

Service moved in step with the kitchen. Chef Teddy explained each piece briefly before placing it down, and front-of-house staff topped up drinks without interrupting the rhythm.

Halal options are available, and the team handled questions about ingredients with patience and accuracy, which makes a real difference for guests with dietary needs.

This venue suits a range of visits. Couples will find it intimate without feeling formal. Solo diners can sit at the counter and enjoy a front-row view of the chefs at work. Small groups celebrating an occasion will appreciate the curated pace, and it works well for a relaxed business lunch in central London.

A weekday evening or early weekend slot offers the best chance to settle in and watch the kitchen properly.

I would happily return to Maki Nori, and I would recommend it to anyone curious about how a handroll restaurant can feel both refined and approachable.

Meeting Chef Teddy Lee added to the evening; his commitment to the craft was clear in conversation and on the plate. For a quality-focused take on Soho sushi, this is a thoughtful and welcome addition to the area.
